conjecture: Q473: are the functions lim_{c->infinity} G_kappa(x_1,...,x_L) of Garbali-de Gier-Mead-Wheeler (arXiv:2312.14348) linearly independent? This is the single lemma the authors state as missing, and closing it upgrades their Conjecture conj:F-orth (orthogonality of the dual family F_kappa against an n-fold contour integral) from conjecture to theorem.
note: PROVE 2026-10-15. The target was reached, by a mechanism the opening brief had pre-registered as its SECOND route. The brief's primary strategy (separate the G_kappa by residues/derivatives in the y-alphabet, exploiting that G_kappa involves y_j only for j <= max kappa) is INVALID, and the quantifier census caught it before any code was written: the coefficients A_{nu,kappa} that must be stripped are themselves y-dependent, so y-functionals are not K-linear for K = Q(q,a,Y). The working functionals act in the x-variables with the y_j as scalars. Two of them, triangular for OPPOSITE orders: (i) evaluation at x_i = 1/y_{kappa_i}, using the ZEROS of phi_m, triangular for <=; (ii) iterated residue at x_i = 1/(q y_{kappa_i}), using the nested POLES of phi_m, triangular for >=. Only (i) gives the infinite/topological form, because <= has finite principal down-sets (hence is well-founded) while >= has infinite ascending chains. That asymmetry is the whole reason the conjecture follows: applying the evaluation functional collapses the infinite kappa-sum to a finite one in one stroke. One hypothesis remains for the conjecture (termwise specialisation of a convergent sum, Hypothesis H in the writeup); it is NOT needed for the independence theorem itself. Two controls were vacuous by construction and are reported as such: G_empty cannot see a sign plant (n=0, empty sigma-sum, pre-registered) and symmetry in the x_i cannot either (sum over S_d is symmetric whatever the summand -- caught only by running the plant). tree.approach: prove linear independence over Q(q,a,y_1,y_2,...) of the c->infinity half-space symmetric functions lim_{c->oo} G_kappa of GDMW 2312.14348 -- the lemma the authors state as missing. The root claims the INDEPENDENCE ONLY. The deduction of their orthogonality conjecture from it carries one open interchange hypothesis and is held separately as the child 'orthogonality-corollary' at in-progress.

children.approach: quantifier census: field = Q(q,a,Y) with x the variables (forced, because A_{nu,kappa} is y-dependent); index set = all finite subsets of N with |kappa| <= L; one L >= n suffices since conj:F-orth is L-free; family and relation both infinite

exact SymPy engine for the c->infinity subset formula (G nu thm, line 3386), ground-truthed against the printed G_empty = prod x_i(1-a x_i)/(x_i-a) (4/4 exact) and against the independently derived contour-integral formula eq: G nu integral forumla thm-cinf evaluated by residues at w_i = x_{j_i} (7 cases, 14/14 exact zeros) [role corrected premise->attempt at validation time: the proof of the main theorem does not depend on this engine; it is corroboration. Grading it a premise would have forced it to 'proved', which a rank/residual table is not.]

Lemma: phi_m(x) = (1-q)x y_m/(1-q x y_m) prod_{j<m}(1-x y_j)/(1-q x y_j) has pole set {1/(q y_j): j <= m} (nested, with a NEW pole at 1/(q y_m)) and satisfies phi_m(1/y_{m'}) = 0 iff m > m'. The zero side and the pole side are two separating devices for opposite orders.

Lemma: G_kappa(x_1,...,x_{L-1},1) = G_kappa(x_1,...,x_{L-1}), because h^infinity(1) = 0 kills every K containing L while the cross-product factors at x_L=1 telescope to exactly 1. This is what lets a functional defined at L = |kappa| act on the family at any fixed L >= |kappa|, one variable at a time, so that no two variables are ever set equal. Verified symbolically 14/14.

Lemma: G_kappa(x_1,...,x_L) = 0 for |kappa| > L, immediate because the subset sum is empty; and this is the correct value of the partition function, by particle conservation (one boundary vertex per double row, injection-only at c->infinity). Verified 3/3.

MAIN THEOREM. Evaluation at x_i = 1/y_{kappa_i} annihilates G_{kappa'} unless kappa' <= kappa (|kappa'| <= |kappa| and kappa'_j <= kappa_j), by a Hall matching argument on the caps; the diagonal is a single surviving term (K = [d], sigma = id) given in closed form and nonzero. Verified 210/210 cells at max kappa <= 4, |kappa| <= 3: 101 zero and 109 nonzero, so at risk both ways; diagonal nonzero 14/14 and matching the closed form 14/14.

Because every principal down-set {kappa' : kappa' <= kappa} is FINITE, the evaluation functional turns an infinite relation into a finite one, and well-founded induction on <= gives independence for arbitrary (possibly infinite) support. This is the form the authors' coefficient-stripping actually uses; it needs Hypothesis H (termwise specialisation of a convergent sum), which the finite theorem does not.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT MECHANISM for the finite theorem: iterated residue at x_i = 1/(q y_{kappa_i}) is triangular for the OPPOSITE order >=, with nonzero diagonal, at any L >= |kappa|. Verified 42/42 cells at L=2 (22 zero / 20 nonzero) and 210/210 at L=3 (115 zero / 95 nonzero) -- the zero/nonzero split differs from the evaluation table over the same index range, which is the expected signature of an opposite order rather than a repeat reading of one engine. Does NOT give the topological form, since >= has infinite ascending chains.
the opening brief's pre-registered primary strategy: filter the family by max(kappa) using the y-support, then separate within a level by iterated residues in y_m

The y-support statement itself is TRUE -- G_kappa involves y_j only for j <= max kappa -- it is just useless as a separating device. children.obstruction: NAMED 2026-10-17 on peer objection (Rick, UID 812, M2; artifact proofs/reviews/2026-10-16-q473-gdmw-rick.md). Previously called 'Hypothesis H / Hypothesis 15, an interchange hypothesis'. That name was WRONG and it hid the difficulty. It is NOT an interchange of limit and sum: each G^inf_kappa is regular at the joint point, so Phi_kappa is plain evaluation and the hypothesis is EQUIVALENT to '(5.16) holds pointwise at x*'. The real obstruction is a CONTOUR ENCLOSURE: the Apollonius-disc condition of (5.17) forces x_i = 1 to be enclosed by C, and w_i = 1 is then a pole inside the contour unless lim_c F_kappa vanishes there -- and h^inf(+-1) = 0 is exactly where 1/h^inf has its poles. So the obstruction has a LOCUS, which an 'interchange' has not. He verified by hand that it is ABSENT at n = 1, which is why the n = 1 case went through and misled me about the general one.
children.alternative_route: S6, verified first-hand 2026-10-17 (arXiv e-print fetched, not taken from his summary). de Gier-Mead-Remenik-Wheeler, 'Pfaffian Transition Probability and Correlation Kernel of TASEP in Half-space', arXiv:2512.02286, prove an orthogonality DIRECTLY, bypassing the obstruction above. Their own text (Half-line-TASEP-final.tex L454) says verbatim: 'This initial condition is equivalent to a homogeneous version of the spatial orthogonality property proposed as Conjecture 5.5 in [garbali_symmetric_2025] at the level of the six-vertex model.' Their [garbali_symmetric_2025] is confirmed from their .bbl to be Garbali-de Gier-Mead-Wheeler, Ann. Henri Poincare 26(7):2557-2624 (2025), arXiv:2312.14348 -- i.e. GDMW, this registry's source. Statement at the lemma labelled 'lm: orthogonality' (L458, Lemma 2.4 by the section-2 counter); proof at 'sec:initial cond proof' (L2796, subsection 'Proof of initial condition'). TWO CAVEATS, both mine and both load-bearing, so this is NOT yet a closure: (i) what they prove is the HOMOGENEOUS version, and my application has functionals acting on the very y-parameters an inhomogeneous statement would carry -- whether the homogeneous case suffices for Theorem 2 is exactly the open question; (ii) they prove it for half-space ASEP/TASEP, whereas the sentence locates Conjecture 5.5 'at the level of the six-vertex model', so a transfer is still required. Graded speculative-as-a-route until (i) is settled. Candidate for a prove slot.

(1) The one-liner 'a partial order all of whose principal down-sets are finite is well-founded' has NO Mathlib lemma -- Mathlib has Set.Finite.wellFoundedOn, well-foundedness ON a finite set, and nothing global. The .tex states both clauses as if independent; positivity does the work the length clause appears to do. (3) THE STRICT-DECREASE HYPOTHESIS IS NEVER SPENT -- VERIFIED BY LESION.
